scope: Serial one-shot paced-WAV model/session measurements of the same public/synthetic 42.9-second English fixture. No native ScreenCaptureKit capture, speaker detection, WebSocket transport, or SwiftUI/native rendering. Model loading is reported separately; hot-path timing can still include kernel startup, thread scheduling and thermal/process variability. Full original input reports are retained without rewriting their fields. The separate transport_regression section preserves authenticated loopback WebSocket smoke reports for both directions; it does not expand the model/session latency acceptance metric to native capture or UI.

metric.name: current source revision to complete matching translation
metric.start: first emitted subtitle record for a segment_id/source_revision
metric.end: emitted nonempty preview/final translation with matching source text and revision
metric.interpretation: Only completed current translations enter this latency distribution; source/translated revision counts and all final records are preserved to expose coverage. The benchmark passed field means protocol/final-record checks passed, not that the 300 ms latency target passed.

latency_acceptance.basis: Use the final runtime validation run (370.46 ms), not the earliest/best observed run.

round2_run_variation.interpretation: These are separate runs/probes taken as the implementation and benchmark reporting evolved. Preserve all three results; do not pool them as identical repetitions or select the minimum to claim acceptance. All three medians exceed 300 ms.

reporting_caveats: The initial greedy report predates the operation-filtered model-call summary; its aggregate translation timing includes lifecycle operations. Preserve the raw report and use the final runtime translate-only summary for the final contention assessment.
The fresh R1 repeat has no model-observer trace; null ownership/executor timing is unavailable evidence, not zero delay.

The Metal command-buffer environment probe (MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER=100, MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER=100) differs from fresh R1 in one of four final target strings (segment 1:2); the final runtime matches all four final source and target strings exactly.
ASR/source revision counts differ between runs. Compare final source/target content exactly, while preserving revision identity consistency within each original report.
The original input reports contain fixture SHA-256 and detailed timings but no runtime-source or model-asset hashes. Source-report SHA-256 values added here identify the input JSON files only.

The additional ASR inference_mode probe was not adopted. It recorded 351.73 ms median and 593.94 ms P95; all 42 source revisions received current translations. Its four final source strings match final runtime, while one final target differs in wording/spacing. Different revision/cache histories prevent causal attribution to inference_mode; it missed 300 ms and has worse P95 than final runtime.

transport_regression.scope: Two separate serial one-shot authenticated loopback WebSocket smoke measurements, English to Chinese and Chinese to English. Native capture, speaker detection and UI rendering are excluded. These transport reception timings remain separate from the model/session latency acceptance metric.

runs.scope: Separate one-shot paced synthetic English WAV through the authenticated loopback backend WebSocket IPC. Includes transport reception in this smoke client; excludes native ScreenCaptureKit capture, speaker detection and native UI rendering. These timings are not pooled with the model/session source-revision latency acceptance metric.

report.target_latency_scope: Paced WAV audio-start to backend WebSocket IPC reception in this smoke client; excludes native capture and UI rendering and does not measure end-of-speech. Source-final waits start at first observed matching final source revision, not at the backend's internal ASR completion. Usable targets are nonblank preview/final translations with a nonblank translated source; useful previews also match the current source text and revision.

runs.interpretation: Protocol and final-pair regression checks passed with 63 frames, unauthorized access rejected, no frame rejection/overflow, verified locked model assets and expected tail retained. This is transport regression evidence, not native system-audio acceptance or evidence that the below-300-ms requirement was met.

runs.scope: Separate one-shot paced synthetic Chinese WAV through the authenticated loopback backend WebSocket IPC. Includes transport reception in this smoke client; excludes native ScreenCaptureKit capture, speaker detection and native UI rendering.

report.target_latency_scope: Paced WAV audio-start to backend WebSocket IPC reception in this smoke client; excludes native capture and UI rendering and does not measure end-of-speech. Source-final waits start at first observed matching final source revision, not at the backend's internal ASR completion. Usable targets are nonblank preview/final translations with a nonblank translated source; useful previews also match the current source text and revision.

runs.interpretation: Protocol/final-pair checks passed with 65 frames and no errors, rejection or overflow. The last final segment is near the audio end, retained at idle, and matched to its source revision. No expected reference tail substring was configured; expected_tail_substring_found is null and must not be described as a reference-text tail check passing.

transport_regression.interpretation: Both directions passed protocol/final-pair regression checks, with 63 and 65 frames respectively and zero errors/rejection/overflow. English had an explicit expected-tail substring check; Chinese did not configure one. Neither smoke report establishes native system-audio acceptance or below-300-ms model/session latency.
